notes:
=== mRemoteNG Credential Extraction ===
mRemoteNG stores encrypted connection passwords in confCons.xml — decrypt with Python script.

=== TECHNICAL DETAILS ===
mRemoteNG: remote connection manager aggregating credentials for RDP, SSH, VNC, Telnet, etc.
Storage: %APPDATA%\mRemoteNG\confCons.xml
Encryption: AES-GCM with key derived from master password
Default master password: mR3m (hardcoded when no custom password set)
The Python script mremoteng_decrypt.py handles both default and custom master passwords

=== FINDING confCons.xml ===
  Get-Item $env:APPDATA\mRemoteNG\confCons.xml
  Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users -Recurse -Include confCons.xml -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

confCons.xml structure: XML with Node elements, each containing Name, Hostname, Username, Password (base64-encoded encrypted blob)

=== DECRYPTION — DEFAULT MASTER PASSWORD ===
  python3 mremoteng_decrypt.py -s <base64_password_value>
  → Returns plaintext credential for that connection
  The default password mR3m is tried automatically when no -p flag is given

=== DECRYPTION — CUSTOM MASTER PASSWORD (BRUTE FORCE) ===
Wrong password causes AES-GCM MAC verification failure (not silent wrong result) — detectable:
  for password in $(cat wordlist.txt); do
    result=$(python3 mremoteng_decrypt.py -s <hash> -p "$password" 2>/dev/null)
    [[ $? -eq 0 ]] && echo "Password: $password, Decrypted: $result"
  done

Protected attribute in XML root element: cracking this yields "Password: ThisIsProtected" — not useful
Target Node elements' Password attributes instead for actual credentials

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
confCons.xml with default master password → instant decryption of all stored credentials
mRemoteNG on sysadmin workstation → credentials for all managed servers, network devices, DCs
Decrypted RDP credentials → direct access to servers without further exploitation
SSH credentials in mRemoteNG → pivot to Linux/Unix infrastructure

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
mRemoteNG in installed software (wmic product) → find confCons.xml
confCons.xml in sysadmin home directories or shared network paths (team shares confCons.xml)
Multiple Node entries = multiple server credentials in one file
Sweep all user AppData directories after local admin escalation

name: Pillaging - Decrypt mRemoteNG Passwords
description: mRemoteNG stores connection passwords in confCons.xml encrypted with a hardcoded default key (mR3m). Decrypt them directly, or brute-force a custom master password with a wordlist.

defense.why_it_works: mRemoteNG stores saved connection passwords encrypted in confCons.xml. By default (and for most users in practice), the encryption uses the default hardcoded key (mR3m). The mremoteng_decrypt.py script implements the same AES decryption to recover all saved connection passwords from the XML file without any credentials.
defense.prerequisites: Read access to confCons.xml (typically in %APPDATA%\mRemoteNG). mremoteng_decrypt.py available. Python installed.
defense.impact: Recovery of all saved RDP, SSH, Telnet, and VNC credentials stored in mRemoteNG — typically admin credentials for all managed servers — enabling full lateral movement.
defense.detection: Read access to confCons.xml by non-mRemoteNG process. mremoteng_decrypt.py execution. Transfer of confCons.xml to external system. SIEM: sensitive credential file accessed by unexpected process.
defense.artifacts: File access: confCons.xml read by non-mRemoteNG process | Process: mremoteng_decrypt.py executed | Network: confCons.xml transferred to attacker
defense.prevention: Configure a custom master password in mRemoteNG (Extras > Options > Advanced > Encryption Password) — this replaces the default key. Restrict read permissions on confCons.xml. Store mRemoteNG config on encrypted storage. Regularly rotate credentials in mRemoteNG connections.
defense.misconfiguration: mRemoteNG configured with default encryption key (no master password set). confCons.xml accessible to other local users or backup systems. Admin credentials stored in mRemoteNG without a custom master password.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# confCons.xml with encrypted passwords (default key):
# <Node Password='nHkTL3aLdJYKGi35g...' />

# Decrypt with default key:
python3 mremoteng_decrypt.py -s 'nHkTL3aLdJYKGi35g...'
# Outputs: P@ssw0rd2024!
defense.secure_config:
# Set custom master password in mRemoteNG:
# Extras > Options > Advanced > Encryption Password
# Enter strong master password

# Restrict confCons.xml permissions:
icacls '%APPDATA%\mRemoteNG\confCons.xml' /inheritance:r /grant "%USERNAME%:(R,W)"

# Enable file access auditing on confCons.xml
